# Frozen save format 6 fixtures

These eight files were written and loaded by the unchanged Ribterra 0.8 implementation at source commit `f62cea0b34ad8495d8ce7a598e79f3f2d3f0e290`, before changing its save schema or gameplay rules. They are preparation for the next migration, not evidence that a format-6-to-newer migration exists.

The source commit passed Windows 40/40, Linux 26/26 and UBSan 8/8 in [run 34238060438](https://github.com/fipsyatina/ribterra/actions/runs/34238060438). Fixture capture and verification were performed separately after that CI run using preserved 0.8 headers and SimCore/Foundation libraries. Their SHA-256 values, individual save hashes and initial/final world checksums are in [world_save_v6.provenance.json](world_save_v6.provenance.json).

| Fixture suffix | Initial tick | State to preserve |
|---|---:|---|
| carry | 18 | Physical construction cargo and its reservation |
| waiting | 681 | Successfully delivered wood, pending gathering continuation and 512 retained external path outcomes |
| builder_planning | 253 | Paid construction, replacement worker and queued Work path |
| builder_travelling | 254 | Replacement worker physically travelling to the paid site |
| builder_working | 469 | Replacement worker physically present and making construction progress |
| exhausted | 1720 | Completed delivery and normal resource exhaustion |
| failed | 1880 | Admission deadline exhausted after 41 attempts; stored Wood remains 83 and no Wood cargo remains |
| work_search | 1551 | Partially searched Work batch 15: 4096 work units, 4334 discovered nodes, frontier cursor 4091 of 4334 |

The first six saves are unchanged outputs of the 0.8 `WorkVisualProbe` and `LogisticsVisualProbe`; their original output paths are recorded in the provenance file. The last two were generated by [capture_world_save_v6.cpp](capture_world_save_v6.cpp), linked against the frozen libraries. It loads the original Waiting/Planning saves and uses ordinary ticks and a normal Move order. It never modifies an exported WorldState, a serialized header, or a payload.

[verify_world_save_v6.cpp](verify_world_save_v6.cpp), also linked against those libraries, loads every original, saves and reloads a separate copy, requires byte-identical re-encoding, and compares the entire gameplay checksum at each of 64 subsequent ticks. All eight passed. Undrained path results are deliberately retained on both sides. The two capture scenarios also independently compare 64 resume ticks.

The corresponding `.expected.json` files are decoded with the frozen [schema](../../schemas/baseline/world_save_v6.fbs), using `flatc --json --strict-json --defaults-json`. They retain every decoded field except the large `chunks` array and legacy empty `tiles` vector. Terrain is still present in each binary and covered by its byte hash and world checksum. Expected checksums are unsigned 64-bit integers; use an integer-preserving JSON parser. The provenance records the original Windows schema bytes under `libraries`, and the repository's LF-normalized schema separately under `normalized_lf_schema_sha256`.

To reproduce the helper verification, build the exact source commit separately and preserve its headers and libraries before compiling these helpers. Their local output root is `.deps/v6-capture`; place the eight input saves in its `fixtures` directory. `verify_world_save_v6.cpp` writes only to its `verification` subdirectory. The capture helper refuses to overwrite the two original outputs. Never compile either helper against a newer implementation and then replace these historical fixtures.

When adding the next schema, use these immutable inputs to test exact migration of inventory, work/path correlations, frontier, deadlines, cursors, permanent XP and terminal states. A new profession must start with a neutral assignment, and migration must not revive Failed/Exhausted work or charge construction again. Retain the exact original primary bytes in `.v6.bak` and test malformed legacy payload rejection independently.
